content: Telavancin is an antibiotic that may cause a severe intestinal condition due to an overgrowth of the bacterium Clostridioides difficile (C. difficile). This condition can occur during treatment or even weeks to months after the treatment has been discontinued. Symptoms of this condition may include persistent diarrhea, abdominal pain, or blood/mucus in the stool. If these symptoms occur, contact your doctor immediately. Avoid using anti-diarrheal or opioid medications, as they may worsen the condition. Prolonged or repeated use of telavancin may lead to oral thrush or a new vaginal yeast infection. These are caused by an overgrowth of fungi that are normally present in the body. Notify your doctor if you notice white patches in your mouth, a change in vaginal discharge, or other symptoms of a fungal infection. Serious allergic reactions to telavancin are rare. However, seek immediate medical attention if you experience symptoms such as rash, itching/swelling (especially of the face, tongue, or throat), severe dizziness, or trouble breathing. This is not a comprehensive list of possible side effects. In the United States, contact your doctor for medical advice about side effects. In Canada, consult your doctor for medical advice about side effects. Before using telavancin, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that can cause allergic reactions or other problems. Discuss your medical history with your doctor, especially if you have kidney disease, heart problems (such as QT prolongation), or low levels of potassium or magnesium in your blood. Telavancin may cause a condition known as QT prolongation, which affects the heart's rhythm. This condition can increase the risk of serious irregular heartbeats. The risk of QT prolongation may be higher if you have certain medical conditions or are taking other drugs that can cause QT prolongation. Low levels of potassium or magnesium in the blood can also increase this risk. Conditions such as severe sweating, diarrhea, or vomiting, or the use of certain medications like diuretics (water pills), may lead to low potassium or magnesium levels. Inform your doctor if you experience symptoms such as fast/irregular heartbeat, severe dizziness, or fainting. Telavancin may interfere with the effectiveness of live bacterial vaccines, such as the typhoid vaccine. Inform your healthcare provider about your vaccination history and any upcoming vaccinations. During pregnancy, telavancin should only be used when clearly necessary, as it may harm an unborn baby. Discuss the risks and benefits with your doctor. If you are breastfeeding, it is unknown whether this medication passes into breast milk. Consult your doctor before breastfeeding. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase your risk for serious side effects. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and nonprescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. Telavancin may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as coagulation tests (PT/INR/aPTT) and urine protein tests, potentially causing false test results. Inform laboratory personnel and your doctors that you are using this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or trouble breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. Laboratory and/or medical tests (such as kidney function tests) may be performed while you are using this medication. Keep all medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of telavancin, contact your doctor or pharmacist immediately to establish a new dosing schedule. It is important to receive each dose as scheduled to ensure the medication's effectiveness. For storage, consult the product instructions and your pharmacist for specific details. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. Consult your pharmacist or local waste disposal company for guidance on safe disposal. This information is a summary and does not contain all possible details about telavancin. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs.
